Spark Optimization & Capacity Planning Platform

RoleDesigner and developer
ChallengeSpark jobs run slow because of small coding choices
SolutionAST code analyser, resource optimizer and storage forecaster
Impact47 s → 1.1 s on a sample job (44× faster)

Toolkit that finds why Spark jobs are slow, sizes clusters for an SLA and forecasts when storage runs out. CLI, FastAPI service and browser demo.

  • Code analyser that parses PySpark with Python's AST and checks Spark SQL for 20+ anti-patterns (Python UDFs, full collect(), cartesian joins, missing cache, global sorts, AQE off), each with a fix and a 0-100 health score.
  • Applying its suggestions to a sample sales job cut runtime from 47 s to 1.1 s (44x faster, identical results) on 500,000 rows in PySpark.
  • Resource optimizer recommending executors, cores, memory and shuffle partitions, with a runtime estimate checked against the SLA.
  • Capacity planner that picks a linear or exponential growth model on held-out data and predicts the date storage fills up.
  • AI layer that sends findings to Claude for plain-language explanations and rewritten code, with a rule-based fallback. 23 pytest tests.

NOV 2024 – MAR 2025

Lunar Path Determination

RoleML and algorithms
ChallengeA rover must cross terrain full of craters and boulders
SolutionRandom Forest hazard map plus A* route planning
ImpactHazards crossed: 29 → 0.3; max slope 35° → 12°

Hazard-aware path planning for a lunar rover. A Random Forest predicts where the terrain is unsafe (crater walls, boulders, steep slopes) and an A* planner finds the safest short route. Served through a FastAPI endpoint.

  • Engineered six terrain features per cell (slope, roughness, curvature, local relief, TPI, max nearby slope) from a 640 m x 640 m elevation map.
  • Hazard model on unseen terrain: precision 0.91, recall 0.86, F1 0.88, ROC-AUC 0.98.
  • Across 20 unseen maps, the planned route crossed 0.3 hazard cells on average versus 29 for the shortest route, and cut the maximum slope from 35° to 12° for 15% extra distance.
  • Interactive browser demo: click any start and goal and the planner runs live in JavaScript.
  • 7 pytest tests, Dockerfile and GitHub Actions CI.

Case study

Case study · Spark Optimization & Capacity Planning Platform

Making a Spark job 44× faster

How I built a toolkit that finds why PySpark jobs are slow, sizes clusters for a deadline and forecasts storage, then used it to speed up a real job.

47s → 1.1sruntime, same results
44×faster
43 → 100code health score
23automated tests

1. The problem

Spark jobs are often slow because of small coding choices, not because the cluster is too small. Data teams keep asking three questions: why is this job slow, what resources does it need, and when will storage run out? Each usually needs an experienced engineer to answer.

2. My approach

I built one Python toolkit with three tools that share the same core code, available as a command line, a FastAPI service and a browser demo:

  • Code analyser: reads PySpark with Python's AST and checks Spark SQL for 25 slow patterns, each with a line number, reason and fix.
  • Resource optimizer: applies standard executor sizing rules, sizes shuffle partitions and checks the runtime against an SLA.
  • Capacity planner: forecasts data growth and the date storage fills up.
  • AI layer: sends the findings to Claude for a plain-language explanation and rewritten code, with a rule-based fallback.

3. The experiment

To test it, I wrote a typical first version of a sales report job. The analyser gave it a health score of 43/100 and found 8 issues.

Before · 47 s

@udf(returnType=DoubleType())
def amount_with_tax(amount, rate):
    return float(amount) * (1 + float(rate))

enriched = orders.join(countries, "country_id")
enriched = enriched.withColumn("total",
    amount_with_tax("amount", "tax_rate"))
top10 = enriched.orderBy(F.desc("total")) \
    .collect()[:10]

After · 1.1 s

enriched = (orders
    .join(F.broadcast(countries), "country_id")
    .withColumn("total",
        F.col("amount") * (1 + F.col("tax_rate")))
    .cache())

top10 = enriched.orderBy(F.desc("total")) \
    .limit(10).collect()

4. Results

Both versions ran on the same 500,000 orders with PySpark 4.2 in local mode (median of 3 runs). The results were identical.

ProblemFixWhy it helps
Python UDF for taxBuilt-in column mathsNo Python call per row
collect() of all rows for top 10orderBy().limit(10)Only 10 rows reach the driver
Shuffle join with a tiny tablebroadcast()The big table never shuffles
Same data computed 3 timescache() onceThe work runs once
Adaptive execution offAQE onMerges small partitions
200 shuffle partitions8, sized for the dataFewer tiny tasks

Most of the gain came from removing the Python UDF and the full collect().

5. Key decisions

  • AST instead of text search. Parsing the real code structure means a comment or string that mentions collect() never causes a false alarm.
  • Model chosen on held-out data. The capacity planner hides the last 20% of the history and keeps whichever growth model predicts it better, instead of assuming one.
  • AI as an extra, not a dependency. With no API key or a failed call, the tool falls back to rule-based explanations, so it always works.
  • Honest estimates. The runtime estimate is a simple throughput model, and the docs say it should be calibrated with real job history.

6. Limitations and next steps

The benchmark ran on one machine, not a production cluster, and static analysis cannot see data size or skew. Next, I want to read Spark event logs to find skewed stages and spill, learn throughput numbers from past jobs, and test on a multi-node cluster.
